body.statement:
From a supplied rational interval name \(\mathfrak r\) for \((p,c_M,c_I,\alpha,G)\), construct a positive rational \(L_J\) and, for every admissible rational interval \(I\subseteq[-G,G]\) and \(m\in\mathbb N\), rational endpoints \(\underline J(I,m)\) and \(\overline J(I,m)\), together with finite checkable evaluation witnesses derived from the piecewise-Gaussian Poisson-energy formulas for \(V_0\) and \(V_\gamma\), such that \((L_J,\mathfrak O)\) satisfies every enclosure, width, and point-width requirement of Definition \(\mathrm{interval\mbox{-}oracle}\) for \(J(p,\gamma)\).  In particular, the construction must certify the explicit uniform modulus
\[
 \overline J(I,m)-\underline J(I,m)
 \leq L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)+2^{-m}
\]
and must not take oracle soundness as an input premise.
body.justification: The theorem supplies the missing model-specific sound oracle through a proved global energy modulus and finite rational point-evaluation receipts.
body.gap: No oracle-soundness premise remains; the remaining limitation is computational efficiency, because termination is proved without a sharp worst-case complexity bound.
body.consumer: Together with the generic certificate theorem and the finite-design regret transfer, it yields a checkable staffing recommendation for the stated compact model class.
body.proof_tex:
We construct the rational modulus first and then the point and interval evaluators.

\emph{Step 1: finite rational parameter bounds.}
Because the supplied name is nested, has widths tending to zero, and preserves the strict positivity conditions in Definition \(\mathrm{input\mbox{-}name}\), a finite prefix supplies rational numbers
\[
 0<\lambda_-\leq\lambda\leq\lambda_+,
 \quad 0<\tau_-\leq\tau\leq\tau_+,
 \quad 0<\nu_-\leq\nu\leq\nu_+,                              \tag{1}
\]
together with rational upper bounds \(c_M^+\geq c_M\), \(c_I^+\geq c_I\), a rational lower bound \(0<\alpha_-\leq\alpha\), and a rational upper bound for \(G\).  Define the positive rationals
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 d_-=\lambda_-+\tau_-,\qquad d_+=\lambda_++\tau_+,\qquad
 D_+=\lambda_++\tau_++\nu_+,\\
 q_-=\frac{\lambda_-(\tau_-+\nu_-)}{D_+},\qquad
 q_+=\frac{\lambda_+(\tau_++\nu_+)}{\lambda_-+\tau_-+\nu_-},
 \qquad
 v_*=\frac{2\lambda_-\tau_-}{d_+^3}.
                                                                    \tag{2}
 \end{gathered}
\]
The defining formulas for \(d,D,q,V_0\) and (1) imply
\[
 d_-\leq d\leq d_+,\qquad D\leq D_+,\qquad
 q_-\leq q\leq q_+,\qquad V_0\geq v_*>0.                       \tag{3}
\]
Rational bisection, certified by comparisons of squared rational endpoints, produces positive rationals \(s_q,s_d,s_0\) such that
\[
 s_q^2\geq q_+,\qquad s_d^2\leq d_-,\qquad s_0^2\leq v_*.      \tag{4}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{gamma\mbox{-}energy\mbox{-}lipschitz}\), (3), and (4) give the rational uniform bound
\[
 |V_\gamma'|
 \leq K_V:=\frac{5\nu_+s_q}{d_-^2s_d}.                        \tag{5}
\]

Enumerate positive integers \(H\) and certify, using the rational exponential enclosures constructed below, the strict inequality
\[
 \frac{e^{-H^2/2}}H<\frac{\alpha_-}{2}.                        \tag{6}
\]
This enumeration terminates because its left side tends to zero.  The elementary Gaussian tail calculation
\[
 1-\Phi(H)
 =\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_H^\infty e^{-x^2/2}\,dx
 \leq\frac{e^{-H^2/2}}{H\sqrt{2\pi}}
 <\frac{\alpha_-}{2}                                           \tag{7}
\]
uses integration by parts and \(\sqrt{2\pi}>1\).  Since \(\alpha\geq\alpha_-\), (7) implies \(z_\alpha<H\).  Moreover, (3)--(4) show
\(\sqrt{V_0+V_\gamma}\geq\sqrt{V_0}\geq s_0\).  Differentiating the design objective and using (5) therefore yields
\[
 |\partial_\gamma J(p,\gamma)|
 \leq c_M^++\frac{c_I^+HK_V}{2s_0}.                            \tag{8}
\]
Thus the explicitly constructed positive integer
\[
 L_J=1+\left\lceil c_M^++\frac{c_I^+HK_V}{2s_0}\right\rceil  \tag{9}
\]
is a rational global Lipschitz constant for \(J(p,\cdot)\) on \([-G,G]\).  Equations (1)--(9) are finite rational receipts except for exponential inclusion in (6), whose finite receipt is supplied in Step 4 below; hence this construction is not circular in the interval oracle.

\emph{Step 2: exact one-dimensional point formula.}
Fix a rational \(g\in[-G,G]\).  Let \(w_g\) be the unnormalized density
\[
 w_g(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 e^{-Dx^2/(2q)},&x\leq g,\\
 e^{-dx^2/(2q)-\nu gx/q+\nu g^2/(2q)},&x>g.
 \end{cases}                                                     \tag{10}
\]
Set
\[
 s=-\frac{\nu g}{d},\qquad K=\frac{\nu Dg^2}{2qd},\qquad
 \sigma_D=\sqrt{q/D},\quad\sigma_d=\sqrt{q/d},                \tag{11}
\]
and write \(y_D(x)=x/\sigma_D\), \(y(x)=(x-s)/\sigma_d\), and \(y_g=y(g)\).  Completing the square on the right branch of (10) gives
\[
 w_g(x)=e^K\exp\{-(x-s)^2/(2\sigma_d^2)\},\qquad x>g.          \tag{12}
\]
Direct Gaussian integration now yields the exact normalizer and unnormalized first moment
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Z={}&\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_D\Phi(y_D(g))
 +e^K\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_d\{1-\Phi(y_g)\},\\
 M={}&-\frac qD e^{-Dg^2/(2q)}
 +e^K\left[s\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_d\{1-\Phi(y_g)\}
       +\frac qd e^{-y_g^2/2}\right].                           \tag{13}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(m_g=M/Z\).  For later use define
\[
 A_0(x)=\int_{-\infty}^xw_g(u)\,du,
 \qquad A_1(x)=\int_{-\infty}^xuw_g(u)\,du.                   \tag{14}
\]
For \(x\leq g\), elementary differentiation verifies
\[
 A_0(x)=\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_D\Phi(y_D(x)),
 \qquad A_1(x)=-\frac qD e^{-Dx^2/(2q)}.                        \tag{15}
\]
For \(x>g\), continuity of the integrals at \(g\), (12), and the substitution \(v=(u-s)/\sigma_d\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A_0(x)={}&A_0(g)+e^K\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_d
              \{\Phi(y(x))-\Phi(y_g)\},\\
 A_1(x)={}&A_1(g)+e^K\left[s\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_d
              \{\Phi(y(x))-\Phi(y_g)\}
       +\frac qd\{e^{-y_g^2/2}-e^{-y(x)^2/2}\}\right].        \tag{16}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Let \(\Psi(x)=A_1(x)-m_gA_0(x)\).  By Definition \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\),
\[
 h_g'(x)=-\frac{\Psi(x)}{q\,w_g(x)}.
\]
Since \(\pi_g=w_g/Z\), substitution into the definition of \(V_g\) proves the nonnested integral identity
\[
 V_g=\frac2{qZ}\int_{\mathbb R}\frac{\Psi(x)^2}{w_g(x)}\,dx. \tag{17}
\]
Thus every compact integrand needed for the point evaluator is an explicit composition of rational operations, square roots, exponentials, and \(\Phi\).

\emph{Step 3: certified tail truncation.}
The mode of \(w_g\) is
\[
 x^*=\begin{cases}0,&g\geq0,\\-\nu g/d,&g<0.\end{cases}       \tag{18}
\]
The potential has curvature between \(d/q\) and \(D/q\).  Integrating its derivative from its minimizer therefore gives, for every \(x\),
\[
 w_g(x^*)e^{-D(x-x^*)^2/(2q)}
 \leq w_g(x)
 \leq w_g(x^*)e^{-d(x-x^*)^2/(2q)}.                            \tag{19}
\]
After integrating the lower bound and dividing the upper bound by \(Z\),
\[
 \frac Z{w_g(x^*)}\geq\sqrt{\frac{2\pi q}{D}},
 \qquad
 \pi_g(x)\leq\sqrt{\frac D{2\pi q}}
 e^{-d(x-x^*)^2/(2q)}.                                        \tag{20}
\]
Choose an integer \(R>|g|+|x^*|\) and put \(r=R-|x^*|>0\).  The bound
\(\int_r^\infty e^{-du^2/(2q)}du\leq(q/(dr))e^{-dr^2/(2q)}\), obtained by replacing \(u/r\) by its lower bound one in the Gaussian derivative integral, and (20) imply
\[
 \mathbb P_{\pi_g}(|X|>R)
 \leq B_R:=\sqrt{\frac D{2\pi q}}\frac{2q}{dr}
 e^{-dr^2/(2q)}.                                                \tag{21}
\]
The Poisson-gradient bound in Theorem \(\mathrm{diffusion\mbox{-}poisson}\) consequently gives
\[
 0\leq2q\int_{|x|>R}\{h_g'(x)\}^2\pi_g(x)\,dx
 \leq\frac{2q}{d^2}B_R.                                       \tag{22}
\]
For a rational input box, use \(|x^*|\leq\nu_+|g|/d_-\) and outward-round the right sides of (21)--(22), replacing \(D,q,d\) monotonically by the bounds in (2)--(3) and using a rational lower enclosure of \(\pi\).  The resulting rational upper bound tends to zero as integer \(R\to\infty\), because its polynomial factor is dominated by \(\exp\{-d_-r^2/(2q_+)\}\).  Enumerating \(R\) therefore gives, after finitely many trials, any prescribed rational tail tolerance.

\emph{Step 4: finite rational elementary-function receipts.}
All transcendental enclosures used above have elementary finite rational certificates.  First,
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239),                            \tag{23}
\]
where (23) is verified by the rational tangent-addition formula and the fact that \(4\arctan(1/5)-\arctan(1/239)\in(0,\pi/2)\).  Integrating the finite geometric identity for \(1/(1+t^2)\) gives the alternating power series for \(\arctan x\) and its first-omitted-term remainder, hence nested rational enclosures of \(\pi\).  Positive square roots are enclosed by bisection, and every step is checked by squaring its rational endpoints.  For \(e^x\) at rational \(x\), choose an integer \(M>2|x|\), enclose \(e^{x/M}\) by its Taylor polynomial and the rational remainder bound
\[
 |R_n|\leq\frac{2|x/M|^{n+1}}{(n+1)!},                         \tag{24}
\]
which follows from \(e^{|x|/M}\leq\sum_{j\geq0}|x/M|^j\leq2\), and raise the resulting positive interval to the integer power \(M\).  Hence these exponential intervals shrink effectively to zero width.

For rational \(x\geq0\), integrate the exponential series to write
\[
 \Phi(x)=\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \sum_{j=0}^\infty\frac{(-1)^jx^{2j+1}}{2^j j!(2j+1)}.         \tag{25}
\]
After the terms begin decreasing, the alternating remainder is bounded by the first omitted term; symmetry handles negative \(x\).  Equations (23)--(25), together with rational interval operations, therefore give finite arbitrarily narrow enclosures of \(\Phi(x)\).

Finally, invert \(\Phi\) monotonically on \([0,H]\) to enclose \(z_\alpha\).  The input name supplies shrinking rational enclosures of \(1-\alpha/2\), and (25) supplies shrinking enclosures of every midpoint value.  If disjoint intervals decide the comparison, perform the corresponding bisection.  If they overlap, retain a symmetric bracket whose radius is the comparison uncertainty divided by a positive rational lower bound for
\[
 \phi(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2},\qquad 0\leq x\leq H,         \tag{26}
\]
 obtained from (23)--(24).  Indeed, the difference of two values of \(\Phi\) is the integral of \(\phi\) between their arguments, so this positive lower bound makes the bracket valid.  Refining both input and function receipts makes its radius arbitrarily small, including when exact equality occurs at a tested midpoint.  Thus quantile inversion terminates at every requested width.  Each of (23)--(26) is certified by a finite list of rational terms, a rational remainder inequality, and outward-rounded rational arithmetic.

\emph{Step 5: terminating point evaluation.}
For a requested rational \(g\) and integer \(n\), dovetail four refinements: advance the input-name prefix; increase \(R\) until (22) is below the assigned error budget; lengthen the receipts in Step 4; and refine a rational partition of \([-R,g]\) and \([g,R]\).  On each cell, evaluate the appropriate formula (15) or (16) by outward rational interval arithmetic and enclose \(\Psi^2/w_g\) by its interval range.  The denominator is certified positive: (20) gives a positive lower bound for \(Z\), while (10) and the compactness of the current parameter box give a positive lower bound for \(w_g\) on \([-R,R]\).  The two expressions agree at \(g\), so there is no omitted kink contribution.

Multiplying each cell's rational range by its rational width gives lower and upper Darboux sums for the compact part of (17).  On each of the two closed branches the integrand is jointly continuous in \(x\) and in all parameters in a sufficiently refined positive input box.  Uniform continuity on that compact set implies that the maximum cell enclosure width tends to zero with the mesh and input widths.  The explicit tail bound (22) tends to zero with \(R\).  The elementary-function receipts tend to zero width by Step 4, and the lower denominator bounds keep division and the final square root uniformly continuous.  Therefore the dovetailing search terminates with a rational interval
\[
 P(g,n)=[P_-(g,n),P_+(g,n)]\ni J(p,g),
 \qquad P_+(g,n)-P_-(g,n)\leq2^{-n}.                            \tag{27}
\]
Here \(V_0=2\lambda\tau/d^3\) is evaluated directly, while \(V_g\) is evaluated by (13)--(17), \(z_\alpha\) by monotone inversion, and \(J\) by its defining formula.  A witness for (27) records the finite input prefix, \(R\), all series orders and remainder bounds, the partition, every cell range, both tail bounds, every bisection bracket, and every outward-rounded rational operation.  Hence (27) is a finite checkable evaluation witness, not an assumed real-number oracle.

\emph{Step 6: the interval oracle.}
For an admissible rational interval \(I=[a,b]\subseteq[-G,G]\), let \(g_0=(a+b)/2\), compute the point enclosure
\(P(g_0,m+1)=[P_-,P_+]\) from Step 5, and return
\[
 \mathfrak O(I,m)=
 \left[P_--\frac{L_J(b-a)}2,
       P_++\frac{L_J(b-a)}2\right].                            \tag{28}
\]
For every \(\eta\in I\), integrating the derivative bound (8)--(9) between \(g_0\) and \(\eta\) gives
\[
 |J(p,\eta)-J(p,g_0)|\leq L_J|\eta-g_0|
 \leq\frac{L_J(b-a)}2.                                        \tag{29}
\]
Combining (27)--(29) proves inclusion of \(J(p,\eta)\) in (28).  Its rational width obeys
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \overline J(I,m)-\underline J(I,m)
 &=P_+-P_-+L_J(b-a)\\
 &\leq2^{-(m+1)}+L_J\operatorname{diam}(I)\\
 &\leq2^{-m}+L_J\operatorname{diam}(I).                        \tag{30}
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(a=b\), (28) is just the point receipt and has width at most \(2^{-(m+1)}\leq2^{-m}\).  Thus (9) and (28), with the finite witnesses of Steps 1--5, satisfy every clause of Definition \(\mathrm{interval\mbox{-}oracle}\).  In particular, the moving kink is handled in a rational point evaluation split exactly at \(g_0\); no interval query relies on quadrature across an uncertain kink.  The already established oracle-conditional capacity-certificate theorem may now be applied to this constructed pair, but no part of the present construction assumes its soundness premise.
